decisions.body: Pre-cutover candidate comparison is allowed, but after acceptance only v1 is authoritative; rollback uses Git and the migration report rather than continued dual writes.
decisions.rationale: This protects nuance while respecting the accepted no-dual-authority architecture.
decisions.title: Audited candidate followed by atomic cutover

decisions.body: No accepted object is silently hard-deleted; replacing authority marks dependent objects for review rather than rewriting them automatically.
decisions.rationale: This preserves stable semantic references without turning the current snapshot into an exhaustive history archive.
decisions.title: Hard-delete only non-authoritative mistakes

decisions.body: A checkpoint is an attention boundary, not a whole-delta authority transition.
decisions.rationale: This supports broad high-bandwidth reviews without accidentally authorizing agent-authored findings.
decisions.title: For awareness plus exact Decisions needed

decisions.body: Authority may switch after the complete brainstorming vertical slice—model, tools, turn loop, projections, migration audit, and production command—is validated. Legacy plan/chunk/run are disabled at that switch; execution integration remains deferred rather than using compatibility documents.
decisions.rationale: This enables real dogfooding without dual authority or allowing downstream workflows to follow obsolete contracts.
decisions.title: Switch brainstorming authority; disable old downstream commands

decisions.body: Adopt one durable tracked model per repository as authority for intended outcomes and explicitly accepted decisions and commitments, while storing uncertainty and agent-authored objects with clearly non-authoritative state. Humans retain authority over outcomes, priorities, values, and acceptance. Code and tests remain evidence of implemented reality; differences are explicit divergence to reconcile. Detailed model-aware planning and execution reconciliation remains deferred.
decisions.rationale: Semantic migration rewrite replacing obsolete legacy terminology while preserving the accepted behavior.
decisions.title: Adopt one durable project model as authority

decisions.body: Input channel does not change semantic authority rules, and no command argument is auto-accepted merely because it started brainstorming.
decisions.rationale: This preserves direct-user commitment without turning `/dag brainstorm auth` into an accidental governing requirement.
decisions.title: Seed is authority-eligible only when semantically explicit

decisions.body: Tools never store raw user wording but mechanically prevent accepted semantic prose/scope/rationale from changing without renewed authority. Explicit batch acceptance identifies exact object hashes.
decisions.rationale: This operationalizes direct-user commitment once while protecting it from later agent drift.
decisions.title: Content-bound semantic acceptance receipt

decisions.body: Explicit unambiguous user direction commits once; silence and agent-derived implications never commit; ambiguity or conflict remains unresolved.
decisions.rationale: This preserves low ceremony and human authority simultaneously.
decisions.title: Direct statements commit; derivations require review

decisions.body: Discovery is an active v1 type during brainstorming, not a dormant execution-only placeholder. Research, repository inspection, prototypes, user observations, and later implementation may produce discoveries. A discovery records a new finding and its possible model impact until the agent integrates it into evidence, assumptions, questions, tensions, proposals, scenarios, decisions, or commitments, dismisses it, or defers it. Future execution reconciliation reuses this same type for worker findings but does not define its existence.
decisions.rationale: Prototypes and research are primary evidence-generating activities during mixed-initiative exploration. Restricting discovery to future DAG execution would lose the finding-to-model-change step that brainstorming already needs.
decisions.title: Use discoveries throughout brainstorming and future execution

decisions.body: Direct requirements may become accepted commitments without synthetic decisions. Derived commitments begin not_reviewed and govern only after explicit acceptance. Decisions link selected proposals and derived commitments without duplicating their prose.
decisions.rationale: This is the smallest split that preserves why, chosen tradeoff, and enforceable contract for different views.
decisions.title: Distinct intent, decision, and commitment

decisions.body: Persist one current tracked snapshot containing materially useful typed objects, including active uncertainty and discoveries. Objects carry stable identity, type-specific state, scope, source/provenance, relationships, timestamps, and confidence where meaningful. Git supplies history; the model is not an event log. Focus-session review/presentation state and scratch research remain ephemeral.
decisions.rationale: Semantic migration rewrite replacing obsolete legacy terminology while preserving the accepted behavior.
decisions.title: Keep one current tracked model snapshot

decisions.body: Generated specs distinguish governing effect from active reconsideration without mixing historical/non-current content into current contracts.
decisions.rationale: This matches the accepted rule that reconsideration does not automatically revoke authority while warning readers about potential change.
decisions.title: Include effective content with an Under review marker

decisions.body: Uncommitted checkpoint deltas are computed by snapshot comparison without writing review metadata into the authoritative model.
decisions.rationale: This supports accurate resume and deltas while preserving the model/presentation boundary.
decisions.title: Ephemeral per-session baseline token/projection

decisions.body: Normative spec inclusion never inherits authority through relationships; every emitted semantic body is explicitly accepted and currently effective.
decisions.rationale: This supports stable vocabulary and representative behavioral examples without smuggling agent interpretation into specs.
decisions.title: Accepted intent, concept, scenario, decision, and commitment are spec-eligible

decisions.body: Focus identity is command-owned, stable, resumable, and never confused with creating another authority model.
decisions.rationale: This preserves convenient interactive use and deterministic automation while making the new one-model semantics visible.
decisions.title: Selector plus new/resume/list/stop subcommands

decisions.body: Cross-workstream links are legal and visible; validators enforce endpoint existence, allowed endpoint types, and acyclic supersession.
decisions.rationale: This supports bounded context without duplicating objects or maintaining reverse-link arrays.
decisions.title: Explicit repository/workstream scope plus typed edges

decisions.body: The durable model is the only semantic working state. Ephemeral sessions contain focus, baselines, and presentation packets but no unique project meaning.
decisions.rationale: This preserves continuity and one authority boundary without treating agent-created objects as accepted.
decisions.title: Write coherent findings to the model during exploration

decisions.body: Hot reload, Pi resume, fork, and clone restore the exact focus-session link carried by the Pi conversation branch and keep model brainstorming active after validating the focus file. A brand-new Pi session without a link starts inactive. Forking does not clone, replace, or suspend the focus session. Concurrent interaction with one focus from multiple agents is unsupported and receives no locks, merge protocol, or coordination UX; users are expected not to do it, and stale hash/file conflicts may fail visibly if they do.
decisions.rationale: Pi forks are commonly used to edit an earlier user response and continue the same conversation, so requiring brainstorm reentry would make correction unnecessarily arduous. Supporting deliberate multi-agent use of one presentation focus is not a product goal.
decisions.title: Keep the exact focus active across reload, resume, fork, and clone

decisions.body: Within the trusted local agent and harness threat model, feedback returned through the active Lavish poll protocol is assumed to be human-initiated and is eligible to bind a review-scoped interaction receipt. Do not require an extra Pi confirmation and do not restrict agent-authored rich context to defend against fabricated submissions. Still match feedback to the active review, point, option, and displayed semantic hashes before resolution. Treat accidental automatic submission as a renderer correctness defect covered by conventions and tests, not as an authority-provenance security boundary.
decisions.rationale: A malicious agent or harness already has substantially greater local capability, and the accepted renderer threat model trusts agent-authored local content. Provenance attestation would add friction without defending a material product threat.
sourceRefs: Direct user direction in Lavish renderer review
decisions.title: Treat Lavish protocol feedback as human-initiated

decisions.body: v1 uses a small explicit type union and shared metadata; subtype-specific fields are required only where they enforce material authority or validation behavior.
decisions.rationale: This supports the adopted loop and migration while leaving room to split types after real usage.
decisions.title: Lean typed v1 core

decisions.body: The agent initiates a user-facing review turn when a coherent cluster needs product judgment, evidence materially changes framing, a user preference blocks progress, a contradiction affects governing direction, a material prototype result appears, continuing risks directional drift, the user changes focus or pauses, or the user requests review. A review turn is an attention/presentation boundary—not a Git commit or authority transition—and uses no fixed time, turn, object-count, or token quota.
decisions.rationale: Materiality-based review turns preserve autonomous research and concentrated oversight without checkpoint/commit terminology that implies repository or authority mutation.
decisions.title: Use materiality-based review turns

decisions.body: V1 marks generated files, renders to a temporary location, supports regenerate-and-compare validation, refuses to overwrite unknown targets, protects hand-authored prototype directories, and reports stale generated files conservatively. It does not require a separate generated-file ownership manifest, manual editable regions, reverse synchronization, or automatic deletion machinery; add stronger ownership metadata only after a concrete cleanup or scale need is observed.
decisions.rationale: The one-way model-to-spec boundary needs basic consistency and file-safety checks, but a manifest and elaborate stale-cleanup protocol are premature defensive architecture before dogfooding demonstrates the problem.
decisions.title: Use minimal one-way projection safety without a required manifest

decisions.body: Use a repeating Explore, Consolidate, Stress-test, Commit, Project loop. Consolidation presents Added, Changed, Still unresolved, Possible misunderstanding, and consequences; stress-testing adds boundary/failure cases, contradictions, and alternatives. Commit explicitly disposes exact model objects according to their type-specific lifecycle; silence commits nothing. Oversight projects Current understanding, Model delta, Decision ledger, Unresolved frontier, Consequence, Divergence, and Representative slices.
decisions.rationale: Semantic migration rewrite replacing obsolete legacy terminology while preserving the accepted behavior.
decisions.title: Center oversight on model deltas and consequences

decisions.body: The one model contains project-specific projection structure without making it governing semantic prose; no second hand-maintained routing file exists.
decisions.rationale: This supports functional domains and supporting documents that do not map one-to-one to workstreams while retaining one project-description source.
decisions.title: Projection declarations inside project metadata

decisions.body: Tracked specs are deterministic structural projections of model-owned prose; regeneration is drift-checkable and hand edits do not mutate authority.
decisions.rationale: This yields readable specs, stable diffs, and one semantic source without requiring an LLM for routine regeneration.
decisions.title: Model-owned prose with deterministic structural projection

decisions.body: Sessions are disposable attention workspaces over one authority and may coexist without separate project snapshots.
decisions.rationale: This preserves useful context switching and resume UX without duplicating semantic authority.
decisions.title: Multiple resumable sessions; one active at a time

decisions.body: Package a tested `lavish-axi` version as an optional runtime dependency and isolate executable resolution plus open/poll/end and bounded TOON recognition in one adapter. Spawn through the current Node runtime, support AbortSignal, never call private Lavish HTTP/state internals, and fall back clearly to chat when unavailable or incompatible. Tests use a fake CLI and recorded outputs.
decisions.rationale: Make review behavior reproducible without requiring networked npx at presentation time.
decisions.title: Use a pinned optional Lavish CLI dependency

decisions.body: Content-bound authority is checked per point/object rather than through global optimistic revision rejection.
decisions.rationale: This is safe under content-bound receipts while preserving sparse-response efficiency.
decisions.title: Apply clear unchanged points; preserve stale or omitted points

decisions.body: Discussion state is derived from linked open questions; governing effect changes only through an explicit authoritative transition.
decisions.rationale: This avoids a second review-state axis and prevents casual exploration from destabilizing current contracts.

decisions.body: Clearly labeled read-only status, workers, inspect, tail, validate, and diagram diagnostics may remain solely for pre-cutover artifacts, but cannot create or advance execution. Mutating legacy workflow operations remain removed or unregistered.
decisions.rationale: Semantic migration rewrite replacing obsolete legacy terminology while preserving the accepted behavior.

decisions.body: Migration preserves current authority and unresolved direction, not every legacy workflow object; the audit report explains mappings, omissions, and representative-view comparison.
decisions.rationale: This avoids both context loss and historical-object bloat while making the one-time transformation reviewable.

decisions.body: Add optional `dag_model_present_review` outside the six semantic project-model tools. It presents/resumes/ends the active review through Lavish, marks presentation only from real feedback, and returns bounded feedback to the agent. It never resolves model state or grants authority.
decisions.rationale: Separate presentation transport from semantic authority and allow independent resume/failure handling.

decisions.body: Keep tension as a separate durable type for enduring opposing forces, with active, resolved, deferred, and retired states. Questions remain concrete uncertainties, contradictions, tradeoffs, or reconsideration prompts and may arise from a tension.

decisions.rationale: This preserves discoverability and cross-domain awareness without duplication drift or noisy repeated contracts.

Context reads narrow slices; update cannot grant authority or rewrite accepted semantics; record_direction is the privileged direct-user authority path; review creates hash-bound packets; resolve_review applies independent fresh outcomes; specs previews, checks, and explicitly recovers projections.

decisions.body: Current understanding is durable shared-agent context but never carries a human acceptance receipt or governing authority; only its latest value is retained.
decisions.rationale: This preserves continuity and comprehension evidence without pretending causal prose is deterministic or human-approved.

decisions.body: V1 does not use one universal authority-status enum; validators derive governing authority from object type, type-specific state, and a valid acceptance receipt.
decisions.rationale: This makes invalid states mechanically rejectable while avoiding mandatory metadata that has no meaning for a type.

decisions.body: Render a versioned `ModelReviewTurnProjection` containing project/focus identity, revision/hash, Current understanding, selected delta/frontier summaries, exact active review content, and optional agent-authored presentation blocks. Generate one self-contained package-owned HTML shell at `.ai/model-sessions/<focus-id>/lavish/<review-id>.html`; preserve it while unresolved, resume interrupted polls, honor user-ended sessions, and end/remove it after resolution. Bundle responsive accessible CSS and standard review controls, permit trusted rich presentation blocks, and return capped prompts plus severe layout/session metadata while omitting DOM snapshots by default. Rely on Lavish's window-level Send to Agent control instead of duplicating a send action at the top of the page. Make option cards self-contained with all prose needed for an informed choice and do not expose serialized authority-payload expanders. Support any number of awareness and decision points in one turn, with independently queued sparse outcomes. Always include an explicit Other radio option so the human can move away from suggested choices. Keep a separate response text box available regardless of which radio option is selected, so the human can add context or modification to a suggested option as well as describe Other direction. Proceed with direct production implementation rather than creating a planning DAG for this bounded slice.
decisions.rationale: The renderer's product frontier and vertical prototype are complete; the remaining work is bounded production integration and end-to-end dogfood, which does not justify a separate planning DAG.

discoveries.body:
Planning, chunking, and execution integration details remain deferred until brainstorming is dogfooded.

- Planning and chunking assign relevant prototypes: Prototypes are optional supporting context at the workflow level. Planning agents decide which plan sections reference prototypes. Chunking decides which referenced prototypes are required reading for particular nodes or flow steps.

- Planning begins with the relevant functional spec: Planning begins with the spec.md for the product scope named by the user. Use spec/spec.md to orient or discover domains when scope is unclear, then follow explicit links as needed.

- Let execution report discoveries while the conductor reconciles the model: Plans and DAG nodes reference accepted commitment/scenario IDs and generated slices. Workers may return structured discoveries, evidence, affected commitments/views, conflicts, and proposed responses, but cannot mutate human-owned intent or accepted decisions. The top-level conductor integrates discoveries as proposed/reopened model objects, produces divergence/consequence views, and requests human judgment when direction changes.
discoveries.title: Deferred model-aware planning and execution details

discoveries.body:
Renderer architecture, modality, controls, transport, threat model, and validation seams remain deferred; V1 is chat-only.

- Use fixed semantic and factual tangent badges: Tangent cards may use a fixed semantic vocabulary such as Foundation, Risk, Needs clarity, Contradiction, Integration, and Prototype candidate, plus derived factual badges such as open-question count, Deferred, Partially settled, and New.

- Badges are agent-owned and ignorable: The agent may add, revise, or remove tangent badges as quick informational flags. Users do not edit or approve badges and may ignore them. Badges never constrain tangent selection or become canonical specification authority.

- Show every in-scope tangent in a flat frontier: The tangent selection surface lists every Proposed, Tracked, Active, and Deferred tangent in one flat collection with badges. Out-of-scope and Closed tangents are omitted from the default frontier.

- Keep the datastore renderer-neutral and resolve outcomes directly: The brainstorm datastore contains no Lavish concepts and no raw feedback collection. It stores renderer-neutral questions, proposals, review packets, decisions, and lifecycle state. The agent may present a review as ordinary Markdown or send the same packet to an optional renderer. After any response channel, the agent interprets user meaning and calls dag_brainstorm_resolve_review with semantic outcomes only.

- Review next actions may suggest optional Lavish rendering: dag_brainstorm_review may return a non-binding next suggestion to present the packet as ordinary Markdown or send it to an optional Lavish renderer. The renderer and its feedback transport never become datastore concepts.

- Let the agent choose the most useful question-context representation: The complete brainstorm-turn document may still use a consistent optional Lavish renderer whose stable shell owns Current understanding, navigation, question cards, badges, standard choices, comments, and turn-level actions. Within each question/review point, the freeform context section is flexible rather than one mandatory renderer-neutral shape: the agent may use ordinary Markdown, predefined semantic blocks, arbitrary HTML/CSS, scripts, or a linked/generated artifact such as an interactive web UI mockup. The workflow must not force every context section to be expressible in every renderer.

- Treat agent-authored brainstorm context as trusted local content: Do not require fragment sanitization, sandboxing, Shadow DOM, CSS scoping, or a security allowlist for agent-authored brainstorm context. The workflow assumes the user and agent are the local authors/readers. Renderers may still apply ordinary layout containment, diagnostics, or namespacing for usability, but not as a restriction on expressive capability.

- Allow fully interactive agent-authored context: Agent-authored context may include scripts, forms, editable controls, interactive prototypes, custom buttons, visualizations, and direct renderer integrations when they help communicate or test an idea. Renderer-provided review controls remain available for common decisions but are not the exclusive interaction mechanism. Any response delivered through custom context is still interpreted by the agent; verbatim responses and unprocessed submissions are not persisted in brainstorm state.

- Require session-level modality choice, not per-context fallback parity: A context section does not require a decision-complete Markdown fallback and rich rendering may carry modality-specific information. The workflow itself must not require Lavish: when the user or agent chooses a Markdown-only session, the agent provides suitable Markdown, a crude textual mockup, or a link to a separately opened artifact. Behavioral compatibility is chosen for the current interaction rather than imposed on every authored context section.

- Offer a small optional semantic component vocabulary: Provide markdown, callout, code, table, comparison, diagram, and freeform context helpers for common presentation. Renderer-owned review cards, understanding, options, recommendations, comments, navigation, and submission remain convenient defaults. These helpers reduce boilerplate but never limit the agent from authoring arbitrary HTML/CSS/scripts or linked artifacts when a brainstorm needs more expressive context.

- Explore the turn-to-Lavish rendering engine in a separate tangent: Do not settle the detailed renderer test contract inside production validation yet. Create a dedicated tangent for the engine that converts Current understanding, turn shell, review points, standard controls, and freeform question context into a whole-document Lavish artifact and transports submissions back to the agent. Define automated renderer validation after that engine's architecture and seams are understood.
discoveries.implications: The renderer frontier is settled for a bounded vertical implementation: a separate presentation adapter, tested optional Lavish CLI dependency, whole-turn projection/shell/lifecycle, bounded human-initiated feedback, and semantic resolution through existing model tools.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Implement and dogfood a vertical renderer prototype before refining secondary shell components or broader renderer automation.
discoveries.title: Deferred turn-to-Lavish renderer details

discoveries.body: The first real open detected the visually hidden skip link as viewport-unreachable and detected exact authority payloads nested inside radio labels as clipped text. Moving details outside labels and using a standard clip-path skip-link pattern removed the findings. Fixture/string scenarios had passed before the browser audit, so production validation should retain one real-browser layout gate in addition to deterministic renderer tests.
discoveries.title: Lavish browser audit catches control failures invisible to string tests

discoveries.body: Implementation exposed and resolved several details that were too small for product-level review: standard controls must carry review, point, option, and semantic hashes; entering freeform text alongside a selected option is a modification, not acceptance; real Lavish output may encode homogeneous warnings as compact TOON tables; resume must render/open when disposable files are missing; user-ended state must survive review rerendering; exact payload disclosure belongs outside radio labels to avoid clipped interactive content; and the browser layout gate catches failures deterministic string tests miss. These are now executable prototype behavior.
discoveries.title: Prototype resolves the first concrete renderer seams

discoveries.body: When a representative second decision was added to prove multi-decision rendering, the human reasonably asked whether its feedback-cap question was fake and selected another fixture option. Although prototype documentation already said the artifact was non-authoritative, the page itself looked like an active review. The sample now carries a prominent Prototype fixture status and notice that queued choices validate interaction only and never resolve the repository model. Representative questions explain which part is illustrative and why the underlying production concern exists.
discoveries.title: Interactive renderer fixtures must be unmistakably non-authoritative

discoveries.body: `dag_model_review` returns the exact review Markdown as a visible tool result, but the Pi adapter marks presentation only when a later assistant text message contains the entire Markdown verbatim. The user responded to the visible review, yet `dag_model_resolve_review` rejected it as unpresented. The manual recovery used the domain presentation marker. Production should recognize the exact tool result/turn delivery itself, or store a tool-result-bound presentation receipt, rather than require a large verbatim assistant echo.

evidence.body: The renderer owns the stable whole-turn shell; freeform question context may be Markdown, helpers, arbitrary HTML/CSS/scripts, or linked artifacts. Lavish is optional, review state remains renderer-neutral, review presentation blocks/waits through dag_brainstorm_review, submissions return to the agent for interpretation, failures leave review active, and detailed automated renderer tests follow the engine architecture.
evidence.title: workflow.md, tools.md, pi-integration.md, and production-validation.md

evidence.body: Dogfood artifacts demonstrate useful whole-turn sections and controls, but their shell, CSS, JavaScript, option forms, navigation, and queuePrompt wiring were repeatedly handwritten by the agent. This confirms the token/consistency value of a renderer-owned shell while preserving arbitrary agent-authored context inside cards.
evidence.title: .lavish/t1-working-surface.html and .lavish/t8-rendering-boundary.html

evidence.body: Lavish 0.1.43 exposes file-oriented open, poll, end, export, and share CLI commands. Open canonicalizes the HTML path and derives a stable session key from it; saving the same file live-reloads the artifact. Poll waits for normalized prompts, user/agent end state, or browser-proven severe layout warnings. Interrupted polls can safely resume because queued feedback persists. User-ended sessions refuse ordinary reopen and require an explicit `--reopen`.
evidence.title: lavish-axi 0.1.43 help and installed implementation

evidence.body: In Lavish 0.1.43, `window.lavish.queuePrompt` posts a prompt from the artifact iframe and `sendQueuedPrompts` submits the queue. Poll normalizes uid, prompt, selector, tag, text, and optional target, but carries no origin or trusted-user-gesture field. Agent-authored scripts share the page and can call the same functions or imitate standard tags. Therefore a poll prompt proves browser-channel feedback was queued, but cannot mechanically prove a human initiated it.
sourceRefs: lavish-axi 0.1.43 injected SDK queuePrompt and normalizePrompt implementation
evidence.title: Lavish poll does not distinguish human-triggered from artifact-script prompts

evidence.body: The artifact receives `window.lavish.queuePrompt`, `sendQueuedPrompts`, and `endSession`. `queuePrompt` emits prompt text plus normalized tag/text/selector/target context; `options.data` is appended as JSON inside prompt text rather than returned as a distinct field. Poll may also return whiteboard references, session-ended metadata, a DOM snapshot, and severe layout warnings. Standard controls should queue one final response per question. A project adapter must cap prompts/bytes and omit the DOM snapshot by default before model context.
sourceRefs: lavish-axi queuePrompt/poll implementation and T8 dogfood
evidence.title: lavish-axi queuePrompt/poll implementation and T8 dogfood

evidence.body: Lavish 0.1.43 ships only a `dist/cli.mjs` executable: package metadata declares no main or exports and documents no JavaScript or JSON API. Results are AXI/TOON. Direct server endpoints and state files are private implementation details. A production adapter therefore needs a pinned CLI subprocess seam, bounded output handling, executable discovery, abort behavior, and fake-CLI tests unless Lavish adds a machine API.
sourceRefs: lavish-axi package metadata and CLI implementation
evidence.title: lavish-axi package metadata and CLI implementation

evidence.body: The renderer maps every review point into its own card and form, uses point IDs as independent queue keys, and the updated fixture visibly renders two decisions in one turn. Each form has suggested radios, an explicit Other radio, and a separate response box available under every selection. Automated scenarios assert two decision forms, two Other paths, and two independent response fields. The user exercised one decision through real Lavish feedback without affecting the other.
evidence.title: Renderer prototype queues multiple decisions with independent open responses

evidence.body: The user-requested prototype under `spec/prototypes/lavish-turn-renderer/` renders a versioned fixture into a deterministic self-contained whole-turn shell; supports Current understanding, delta, frontier, awareness, decisions, exact payloads, and trusted interactive HTML; bounds expanded and compact-table CLI feedback; and exercises fake open/poll/end, missing-artifact open, abort/resume, user-ended preservation, and cleanup. Standard controls carry review/point/option hashes and treat any freeform text as modification. The real Lavish browser audit initially found one unreachable skip link and two closed-details clipping failures; the shell was corrected and fresh polls returned waiting with no layout warnings. Project smoke and deterministic spec checks pass.
evidence.title: Bounded Lavish turn-renderer prototype passes vertical scenarios

evidence.body: Pi custom tools execute after runtime initialization with an AbortSignal, incremental `onUpdate`, and extension context. A presentation adapter tool can spawn Lavish open/poll, report that the browser is waiting, remain attached to the current agent turn, kill only the poll subprocess on abort, and later resume the same file-keyed Lavish session. Session start/reload hooks can restore focus presentation metadata without starting background resources during extension loading.
sourceRefs: Pi extensions.md custom-tool and lifecycle contracts
evidence.title: Pi tools can host an interruptible Lavish review wait

currentUnderstanding.body: The renderer product frontier and vertical prototype are complete. The user explicitly authorized leaving brainstorming and implementing the bounded production slice directly without a planning DAG. Governing behavior includes a live model-owned turn projection, separate optional Lavish presentation tool, deterministic resumable artifact lifecycle, one host send surface, self-contained option prose, independent multi-point outcomes, explicit Other plus a separate response box, bounded feedback, automatic exact presentation recognition, semantic resolution through existing tools, and cleanup after resolution. The focus is being suspended while implementation proceeds.

proposals.body: The tool supplies state references, and the agent authors the full shell, styles, scripts, controls, and context.
proposals.rationale: This maximizes page freedom but retains repeated shell/control tokens and inconsistent review behavior.
proposals.title: Let the agent provide complete HTML

proposals.body: Spawn `npx -y lavish-axi` from the adapter and rely on the npm registry/cache for installation and version selection. Parse the current TOON output and fall back to chat on command failure.
proposals.rationale: Keeps Lavish out of package dependencies and mirrors the current skill workflow.
proposals.title: Invoke ambient npx Lavish on demand
tradeoffs: May access the network during a review.
Version drift can break output recognition without a project change.
npm/npx availability becomes an undeclared runtime requirement.

proposals.body: Standard controls queue prompts naming review ID, point ID, proposed action, option ID, and the displayed semantic hash/payload. The adapter returns only normalized prompts, tags, text/targets, user-ended state, and severe layout warnings; it drops the DOM snapshot unless explicitly requested, caps prompt count and total bytes, and uses Pi truncation metadata when needed. Within the trusted local agent/harness threat model, feedback returned through the active Lavish poll is assumed human-initiated and may create a review-scoped interaction receipt. The agent still interprets all feedback and calls `dag_model_resolve_review`; matching active review IDs and semantic hashes prevents stale or misrouted outcomes.
proposals.rationale: This preserves correction and ambiguity handling while preventing arbitrary DOM state from flooding model context or bypassing semantic review.

proposals.title: Return bounded Lavish feedback for agent interpretation
tradeoffs: Agent interpretation adds a model turn and can ask clarification.
Annotations and custom controls remain less mechanically structured than standard options.
Truncation must never silently turn partial feedback into authority.

proposals.body: Return session/artifact references, session-ended status, normalized prompts with prompt/tag/text/selector/target and whiteboard summary/file references, plus severe layout warnings. Omit the DOM snapshot and server chatter from routine model content; save diagnostics by reference only when needed. Standard shell controls queue stable review-point/proposal IDs and human-readable labels. The agent interprets the packet and calls resolve_review; no transport field is persisted automatically.
proposals.rationale: The packet preserves user intent and precise annotation targets while excluding large page snapshots and operational prose that provide no routine reasoning value.
proposals.title: Return a bounded intent-transport packet, not raw poll output

proposals.body: If explicitly requested, create `spec/prototypes/lavish-turn-renderer/` with a fixture-driven `ModelReviewTurnProjection`, package-owned self-contained shell, standard sparse decision controls, trusted rich-context examples, deterministic focus/review artifact path, bounded feedback normalization, and fake Lavish open/poll/end scenarios. Include one opt-in live Lavish exercise. Do not register a production tool or mutate project-model authority from the prototype. Use the concrete result to refine projection fields, lifecycle states, limits, accessibility, and failure recovery before implementing the production adapter.
proposals.rationale: The broad product direction is settled; remaining uncertainty concerns concrete seams best exposed by a runnable artifact rather than more abstract review.
proposals.title: Build a bounded vertical Lavish turn-renderer prototype

Avoids prematurely coupling production code to an untested projection/shell contract.
Must remain bounded and not become a second authority implementation.

proposals.body: Build the turn document as a hydrated framework application with packaged JavaScript and CSS assets.
proposals.rationale: This supports sophisticated components but adds a browser build pipeline, hydration/runtime complexity, and less transparent artifacts.
proposals.title: Ship a compiled client-side application bundle

proposals.body: Generate one self-contained HTML document from package-owned template, CSS, and standard control JavaScript; do not require Tailwind, DaisyUI, or remote assets at runtime. The shell owns navigation, Current understanding, awareness and decision cards, exact authority payload disclosure, recommendations, comments, queue/send actions, and responsive layout. Agent-authored presentation blocks may use Markdown, predefined components, trusted HTML/CSS/scripts, or links to sibling artifacts without a restrictive sandbox.
proposals.rationale: Bundling removes network/version drift and repeated shell boilerplate while preserving the accepted trusted-local expressiveness boundary.
proposals.title: Bundle a stable offline shell and allow trusted rich context
tradeoffs: Arbitrary context can still disturb shell usability, so layout diagnostics and conventions remain useful.
A bespoke shell needs accessibility and responsive tests.
Linked artifacts require relative-path and size safety.

proposals.body: Standardize the current artifact approach around browser-loaded Tailwind and DaisyUI versions.
proposals.rationale: This provides a broad component library quickly but requires network availability and a browser CSS compiler for the standard shell.
proposals.title: Generate a DaisyUI/Tailwind CDN shell

proposals.body: Write the renderer-owned HTML to `.ai/model-sessions/<focus-id>/lavish/<review-id>.html`. The canonical path gives Lavish stable session identity and live reload. Store only presentation metadata in the ignored focus session: review ID, relative artifact path, status, last presentation hash, and whether the user ended the browser session. Preserve it while the review is unresolved; end and remove it after resolution. An interrupted poll resumes. A user-ended session falls back to chat unless the user explicitly requests reopen.
proposals.rationale: The artifact is disposable presentation state while unresolved meaning stays in the repository model and active review packet.
proposals.title: Use one deterministic ignored artifact per focus review
tradeoffs: Removing a resolved artifact loses the local visual record, which is intentionally non-authoritative.
User-ended state must be tracked to honor Lavish reopen etiquette.
Focus cleanup needs best-effort CLI end plus file removal.

proposals.rationale: This avoids package dependency weight but creates version drift, network behavior, and less reproducible integration.
proposals.title: Require a global command or run npx latest

proposals.body: Promote the validated seams into production modules: a domain-owned `ModelReviewTurnProjection` generated from the actual active focus, model revision/hash, Current understanding, selected frontier/delta, and exact active review; optional focus presentation metadata; package shell renderer; pinned optional Lavish CLI adapter; active `dag_model_present_review` tool with present/resume/end; bounded feedback details; exact tool-result presentation receipts; resolution cleanup; fake-CLI tests; and one opt-in real-browser gate. Reuse contracts deliberately rather than importing prototype modules. Production dogfood is complete when one real multi-point model review is generated, presented, responded to, semantically resolved through existing tools, and cleaned up without manual presentation-marker recovery.
proposals.rationale: The broad decisions and first concrete seams are settled; another abstract pass is unlikely to reduce more risk than production dogfood.
proposals.title: Implement the production Lavish presentation adapter from prototype findings
tradeoffs: Production integration will expose additional Pi lifecycle details.
The prototype remains evidence and should not become a runtime dependency.
A user visual pass may still request shell iteration before or during production work.

proposals.body: Extend `dag_model_review` with a presentation mode. In Lavish mode the semantic tool creates the review, renders and opens the artifact, waits for feedback, and returns it to the agent; resume/end actions are also folded into that tool.
proposals.rationale: One agent call creates and presents a review and keeps the active tool list at six.
proposals.title: Integrate Lavish presentation into dag_model_review
tradeoffs: Conflates semantic packet creation with an optional long-running presentation transport.
Resume and layout-repair actions complicate the existing review schema.
A CLI failure becomes a failure of the semantic review tool.

proposals.body: Treat Lavish poll results as non-authoritative user feedback and presentation evidence. The agent interprets and summarizes selected reviewed outcomes in Pi chat, then asks the user for one explicit confirmation. Only that Pi input creates the interaction receipt used by `dag_model_resolve_review`. Lavish can still drive awareness, annotations, corrections, navigation, and proposed sparse outcomes without authority. A later trusted-action protocol could remove the confirmation step.
proposals.rationale: This preserves unrestricted rich context and the current mechanical authority boundary without relying on provenance Lavish does not provide.
proposals.title: Require Pi confirmation before Lavish feedback grants authority
tradeoffs: Adds one short Pi confirmation after browser review.
The browser cannot be the sole decision channel in V1.
Safe to ship against current Lavish without upstream changes.

proposals.body: Declare lavish-axi as an optional compatible dependency and isolate open/poll/end subprocess calls in one adapter. Invoke through Pi's abort-aware execution, parse official AXI/TOON output with an explicit parser dependency, and never call private HTTP endpoints. If absent or incompatible, report a renderer error and preserve the active review. Replace this seam if Lavish later exports a stable JavaScript or JSON API.
proposals.rationale: This uses the supported public interface without requiring a user-global install, npx latest/network behavior, or coupling production code to private server routes.
proposals.title: Use an optional pinned Lavish CLI behind a replaceable protocol adapter

proposals.body: Write atomically to .ai/brainstorm/render/<brainstorm-id>/<review-id>.html. Re-rendering the same review updates that file for Lavish live reload. dag_brainstorm_review supports presenting/resuming the existing active review after interruption without creating a new packet. Poll runs in the foreground with the Pi abort signal; interruption leaves review/session resumable. Resolution best-effort ends the Lavish session and deletes the artifact; archive removes leftovers. User-ended sessions are not reopened unless explicitly requested.
proposals.rationale: Path-derived identity avoids Lavish metadata in the datastore, supports one live session per review, and prevents stale ended sessions or historical artifacts from becoming another state/history layer.
proposals.title: Use one derived ephemeral artifact per active review

proposals.body: Treat Lavish as an optional runtime capability. Resolve a package-installed `lavish-axi` executable pinned to a tested version, spawn it through the current Node executable, and isolate open/poll/end plus TOON status recognition in one adapter module. If unavailable or incompatible, report a clear chat-fallback result. Do not call private HTTP endpoints or read Lavish state files. Tests use a fake executable and recorded bounded outputs.
proposals.rationale: Lavish currently offers no public JavaScript or JSON API; one subprocess seam minimizes coupling and prevents ambient `npx` network/version drift.
proposals.title: Use a pinned optional Lavish CLI dependency behind one adapter
tradeoffs: Pinning requires deliberate upgrades when Lavish evolves.
An optional dependency increases install size when present.
Minimal TOON recognition is still a protocol dependency until an upstream machine API exists.

proposals.body: Start/locate the server and use its internal sessions, poll, reply, and end endpoints from the extension.
proposals.rationale: This avoids parsing CLI output but couples production behavior to undocumented routes and server-state details.
proposals.title: Call Lavish server HTTP routes directly

proposals.body: Pass prompts, DOM snapshot, layout data, server guidance, and all metadata directly into the tool result.
proposals.rationale: This preserves all diagnostics but spends context on repeated page structure and operational guidance.
proposals.title: Return complete Lavish poll output

proposals.body: Pass only brainstorm/review IDs and let renderer code query and select whatever it needs.
proposals.rationale: This centralizes projection logic but couples rendering to the datastore and broadens its authority/data surface.
proposals.title: Let the renderer read complete brainstorm state

proposals.body: Define a renderer-neutral `ModelReviewTurnProjection` containing project/focus identity, model revision/hash, non-authoritative Current understanding, delta/frontier summaries selected for this turn, the exact hash-bound active review points/options/dispositions, and optional agent-authored presentation blocks. The renderer receives this projection from the domain adapter and never reads `project-model/model.json` or full focus state directly.
proposals.rationale: A stable input contract lets chat and Lavish share semantic review content while the renderer owns layout and the domain owns model access.
proposals.title: Render from a narrow versioned turn projection
tradeoffs: The projection becomes a versioned API that requires fixtures.
Agents need an explicit way to attach rich presentation blocks.
Large context blocks require size limits or linked artifacts.

proposals.body: Map selected proposal IDs and comments to decisions inside renderer/adapter code and call resolution automatically.
proposals.rationale: This is efficient for simple choices but cannot safely interpret corrections, contradictions, custom context, mixed comments, or changed rationale.
proposals.title: Translate standard controls directly into semantic state

proposals.body: For a single-channel Lavish authority flow, render exact review choices only through package-owned shell controls and disallow arbitrary agent-authored scripts in the same authority document. Rich scripted context must be linked as a separate artifact that cannot call the review queue. The adapter may then treat standard action prompts from its trusted generated document as review-scoped human interactions.
proposals.rationale: Constraining executable context makes the generated authority surface a trusted code boundary despite Lavish lacking prompt-origin provenance.
proposals.title: Restrict authority review surfaces to package-owned controls
tradeoffs: Reverses the accepted unrestricted-context-in-one-document direction.
Rich context and decision controls become separate browsing surfaces.
Still relies on trusted renderer and Lavish package code.

proposals.body: Do not add production renderer code. Continue using the Lavish skill and bash commands to author ad hoc review artifacts when useful; ordinary `dag_model_review` remains chat-only.
proposals.rationale: Avoids dependency and adapter complexity until more dogfood establishes recurring renderer requirements.
proposals.title: Keep Lavish as an agent skill only
tradeoffs: Repeats shell/CSS/control boilerplate and burns context.
No deterministic focus/review resume behavior.
Authority confirmation remains entirely manual.

proposals.body: Write review documents under .lavish/ and retain them after resolution for later browsing.
proposals.rationale: This aids retrospective browsing but creates a second history surface and conflicts with disposable projections.
proposals.title: Keep one .lavish artifact per review as history

proposals.body: Implement server-side TypeScript template/components for understanding, navigation, frontier, review cards, recommendations, Other/comments, queue/submit state, and turn actions. Generate a portable HTML document with package-owned inline CSS and control JavaScript; freeform context may load its own dependencies. Avoid a browser build step and avoid requiring Tailwind/DaisyUI CDN for the standard shell.
proposals.rationale: Generated boilerplate costs no model tokens, works offline, stays visually consistent, and avoids CDN/runtime failure while keeping final artifacts ordinary editable HTML.
proposals.title: Ship a self-contained package-owned shell

proposals.body: Add an optional `dag_model_present_review` tool outside the six semantic project-model tools. It accepts the active review ID and an action such as present, resume, or end; renders the renderer-neutral review projection; opens or resumes Lavish; waits through poll; marks the exact review presented only when browser feedback proves delivery; and returns bounded feedback for agent interpretation. It never resolves review state or grants authority.
proposals.rationale: This preserves the six-tool authority boundary and lets Markdown and Lavish present the same review packet without making Lavish a datastore concept.
proposals.title: Keep Lavish as a separate presentation adapter tool
tradeoffs: A seventh active tool increases surface area.
The agent performs a second tool call after creating a review.
Presentation and semantic resolution remain mechanically separable.

proposals.body: Every review rewrites one stable file and continues or reopens the same Lavish session.
proposals.rationale: This minimizes files and supports continuous reload, but ended-session state and old annotations can leak across semantically distinct reviews.
proposals.title: Use one current.html for the whole brainstorm

proposals.body: The domain supplies one TurnProjection containing brainstorm/revision identity, Initial/Current understanding, active review points and stored options, selected frontier summaries, and explicitly relevant settled context. Each point chooses context kind: Markdown, semantic helper blocks, trusted raw HTML/CSS/scripts, or linked/embedded artifact. The renderer never reads full brainstorm state and the agent never authors the standard document shell.
proposals.rationale: A narrow projection preserves datastore/renderer separation and sensible context use, while explicit context kind lets the engine insert unrestricted material correctly without forcing cross-renderer compatibility.
proposals.title: Render a narrow turn projection with explicit flexible context descriptors

proposals.body: Ask Lavish to expose a machine-readable poll mode and a chrome-owned trusted-action control path that binds a user gesture to opaque action data without making the token callable or forgeable by artifact scripts. If such provenance can be audited, the adapter could create a review-scoped interaction receipt and resolve exact displayed options without a Pi confirmation round trip.
proposals.rationale: This is the only path identified so far to retain unrestricted artifact scripts and make Lavish the sole authority channel mechanically.
proposals.title: Explore an upstream trusted-action protocol for single-channel authority
tradeoffs: Depends on upstream design and release timing.
Browser gesture/provenance security needs careful threat modeling.
Not required for an initial presentation-only adapter.

questions.body: Should V1 treat all Lavish feedback as non-authoritative input requiring explicit Pi-chat confirmation, constrain rich context around authority controls, or depend on a future Lavish protocol that distinguishes trusted human actions from artifact-script submissions? Any choice must prevent agent-authored scripts from manufacturing acceptance while preserving useful visual review.

scenarios.body: When the user forks or clones a Pi conversation to edit an earlier response, the exact linked focus session is validated and remains active without requiring `/dag brainstorm` reentry.
scenarios.title: Forking to correct an earlier response preserves focus

scenarios.body: When the user answers only part of a review and unrelated model content changed, each fresh hash-matching point resolves independently while omitted, ambiguous, contradictory, or stale points remain unresolved.
scenarios.title: Sparse review resolution preserves stale and omitted points

tensions.body: The accepted renderer boundary allows trusted agent-authored HTML, scripts, forms, and custom controls, but human authority requires that agent code cannot manufacture an eligible acceptance interaction. Lavish currently gives artifact scripts and visible controls the same queuePrompt channel with no trusted-gesture provenance. Preserving both unrestricted scripting and direct browser-to-authority resolution is therefore unsafe without another confirmation or protocol boundary.
tensions.title: Unrestricted rich context versus mechanically trustworthy authority input
